title: Meridian Labs - Onboarding Planning Huddle
summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding with Meridian Labs. Aligned on network/VPC needs, data retention, SLA expectations, basic rollout plan (dev->staging->prod), and a small pilot focused on chat assistants for customer ops. Priya outlined runtime and quantization options; Samir asked for SOC2 artifacts and KMS details. Agreed next steps: share security packet, sample infra diagram, setup pilot project and credentials, schedule 1-week benchmark window.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-29 15:00 PST | Duration: 56m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Patel, Aisha Gomez (Redwood) / Carlos Mendes, Lena Brooks, Samir Rao, Maya Ortiz (Meridian Labs)

Summary (auto): Quick onboarding planning, security rubrics, pilot scope, network needs.

00:00 Jordan Lee: hey thanks everyone for carving out time today, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick roll call?
00:07 Carlos Mendes: hi this is carlos, cto,/ on my side lena and samir and maya are here.
00:13 Jordan Lee: awesome, thanks. priya would you like to kick off with a quick tech overview?
00:18 Priya Patel: sure yeah, hi all. so i want to run through three things quickly — runtime options, connectivity and the pilot scope. um first, runtime: we offer hosted api, dedicated pools, and private vpc deployments. for pilot most customers start on hosted or dedicated for predictable throughput. there are tradeoffs — dedicated gives you reserved gpus, predictable p95 latency, and private gives you customer-managed networking plus k m s integration.
00:46 Lena Brooks: can you clarify private? like is it a fully airgapped on prem option or vpc peering?
00:52 Priya Patel: good question. private can be either. we have a v p c peering flow for cloud customers —— that's most common, the on-prem package is heavier and tends to be for regulated workloads. it also supports hsm-based k m s via our integrations, but we can go into the specifics in the security packet.
01:12 Samir Rao: okay, we'll need SOC 2 and the specific KMS flow. do you support bring-your-own-kms?
01:18 Priya Patel: yes, BYO KMS is supported on Private and on Dedicated through customer key wrapping. sometimes the transcript here says key wrap but it's basically a customer-managed key. we'll put the exact arn examples in the doc.
01:30 Jordan Lee: and just to set expectations on data retention — hosted api stores logs for 30 days by default but we can configure retention or disable logging for enterprise plans — we'll include the options.
01:40 Maya Ortiz: for our legal and privacy team we need a data flow diagram and where logs land, yeah.
01:44 Jordan Lee: noted, we'll attach a network diagram and mapping.
01:48 Priya Patel: moving to pilot scope — we recommend a small footprint: 10k conversations equivalent, two model variants (a smaller quantized model for cost-sensitive flows and a larger model for high quality), and a two-week benchmark window. measure latency p50/p95/p99, throughput errors, and a quality eval on 200 seed prompts.
02:10 Carlos Mendes: sounds reasonable. timeline wise we want something in staging in two weeks if possible.
02:15 Aisha Gomez: that seems doable assuming the VPC peering is quick — lena, is your infra team ready to open up peering?
02:20 Lena Brooks: we can open peering but we need the CIDR ranges and egress IP list. also, do you do static IPs?
02:26 Priya Patel: yes we provide egress IP ranges for firewall allow list, and static IP options are available on Dedicated and Private. we'll send the egress ranges in the network doc.
02:36 Samir Rao: encryption at rest? encryption in transit? what about audit logs retention for sysadmins?
02:41 Priya Patel: transports are TLS1.3, encryption at rest uses AES-256. audit logs are available in the console and can be forwarded to your SIEM (we support S3 / Splunk / Datadog sinks). retention is configurable by tier.
02:56 Jordan Lee: side note — a lot of customers ask about KV cache and batching because they affect cost; priya can share suggestions on quantization and batching profiles later.
03:06 Priya Patel: yeah kv cache warms up session state and helps latency for chat; batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency, so we'll propose a batch config per workload. also quantization: we support 8-bit and 4-bit profiles, 4-bit reduces memory but some edge-case quality regressions, we'll include sample evals.
03:30 Maya Ortiz: what about cost visibility? how granular are the reports?
03:33 Jordan Lee: console gives token-level breakdowns per route and model, and per project. we'll also provide initial cost estimates for the pilot.
03:40 Carlos Mendes: are there any gotchas with our use case — primarily customer support assistants, sensitive PII occasionally.
03:47 Priya Patel: for PII we recommend redaction at ingestion or token-level masking, and Private deployment with BYO-KMS is safest. we also support in-flight token filters if you need to drop PII before it touches the model.
04:05 Lena Brooks: ok good, security triage will want a short checklist of what's needed for peering and what's needed for service account permissions.
04:12 Jordan Lee: action: we'll send a one-page network checklist plus the longer security packet with SOC2, subproc details, and KMS workflows.
04:20 Samir Rao: can you also include the pen test cadence? we need to know if you do third-party pen tests and if results are shareable.
04:27 Priya Patel: we do third-party tests annually; redacted summaries are available, and full reports can be shared under NDA. we'll note that in the packet.
04:38 Carlos Mendes: cool. let's talk success criteria — p95 latency under 400ms for short convs is our bar, and cost target under 0.004 per token equivalent. can you confirm those are realistic?
04:52 Priya Patel: for dedicated pools with appropriate model choice and batching yes, those are achievable. on hosted there's more variability but we can target similar numbers with a slightly larger safety margin.
05:05 Aisha Gomez: next steps i'll open the pilot project and create the initial team access. jordan will follow up on pricing and a sample invoice for dedicated if you choose that path.
05:15 Jordan Lee: yep i'll include pricing scenarios: hosted, dedicated, private with estimated monthly commit and burst.
05:20 Lena Brooks: who will own the pilot on your side?
05:23 Aisha Gomez: i'll be the CSM lead and priya will be the technical lead, jordan for commercial.
05:28 Maya Ortiz: do you have a recommended observability dashboard sample?
05:31 Priya Patel: yes we can share a dashboard template — token usage, latency by model/route, error rates, and KV cache hit ratio.
05:40 Carlos Mendes: any docs I should review now?
05:42 Jordan Lee: i'll post links in the follow-up: kickoff deck, security packet (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/packet/meridian), network diagram (link: https://redwood.example.com/network/diagrams/meridian-sample.pdf), and the pilot runbook draft (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilots/meridian-runbook).
06:00 Samir Rao: noted. earlier you mentioned model variants — is it easy to fall back to a smaller model if latency spikes?
06:08 Priya Patel: yes we support routing policies — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if SLOs are missed. that's configurable per route.
06:18 Carlos Mendes: last question from me — audit logs retention and export, is there an SLA for log export?
06:25 Priya Patel: exports are best-effort but for enterprise we can set up guaranteed export windows and retention policies as part of the contract.
06:33 Jordan Lee: ok i think we're aligned. recap of next steps: redwood shares security packet + network checklist, redwood opens pilot project and invites meridian team, meridian to provide CIDR and service account, schedule pilot kickoff for week of feb 8th.
06:47 Lena Brooks: timeline works for us, we'll try to have CIDR and egress by feb 5th.
06:52 Jordan Lee: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites.
06:56 Carlos Mendes: thanks all, bye.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (KMS sometimes transcribed as K M S or key-mass etc.), and some speaker label alignment may be off — verified medium quality.

Referenced artifacts: kickoff deck (link), security packet (https://redwood.example.com/security/packet/meridian), network diagram (https://redwood.example.com/network/diagrams/meridian-sample.pdf), pilot runbook draft (https://redwood.example.com/pilots/meridian-runbook).
